shifts.summary: Candidates reported a mixed difficulty overall, with many finding the paper harder than expected. Reasoning had many statement based questions and a few coding‑decoding items, while GA was described as difficult by several sources. Quantitative section was largely difficult with many trigonometry and geometry problems. English was generally easy to moderate, though some tough vocabulary appeared.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Statement based questions were numerous, some coding‑decoding and matrix items appeared. Candidates mentioned both easy and tricky reasoning items, with attempts ranging from 22 to 24.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GS portion was reported as hard, with many current affairs and constitutional questions. Some reports noted easy GA items, but the majority described difficulty.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant had a mix of easy and very hard items; many trigonometry, circle geometry and tangent problems were reported.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was generally doable with some tough vocabulary; passage based set was easy for most candidates.

observations: Pattern changed compared to previous years, with more statement based reasoning.
GA was the toughest section for many candidates.
Quantitative section mixed easy and very difficult items, especially trigonometry.
English remained the most approachable section overall.
disagreements: Overall difficulty reports split between Difficult and Easy to Moderate (two reports each).
English difficulty split between Easy and Easy to Moderate (three reports each).

intro: On 22 October 2026, the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted in three shifts. Shifts 1 and 2 have been reported, with Shift 1 described as moderate to difficult and Shift 2 as easy to moderate. The reported good‑attempt ranges are unofficial and the SSC normalises scores across shifts.
